Saran Cling Plus is kind of like most of the Cling Wrap from Glad. It is a very good quality plastic wrap, but the delivery system is poorly executed, and this makes usage more frustrating and less time-efficient. As convenience is one of the core selling points of this sort of product, how easy it is to use is just as important as how good the wrap itself is.

As another user here noted, getting this stuff out of the box and tearing off the portion you need to use is very difficult. Substantial force is required to do this due to a cutting system that is lacking, and this can result in the box being damaged as it is not a very robust box. It can also cause the piece you are attempting to tear off fold up from the pressure upon being torn, leaving you with a tangled mess to untangle. As the blade itself does not do a great job cutting, sometimes the wrap will tear, leaving you with a piece that is a different size than you wanted. The physical location of where the wrap comes out relative to where it is cut at also results in one having to hold at an awkward angle to see what they are doing, making all of this more difficult.

I use clear wrap multiple times a day...the difference between a delivery system that is easy versus difficult means a lot of time savings, and a lot of frustration that does not have to occur. This is a good quality wrap, but like Glad's wrap, it's delivery system is lacking compared to other products (such as the Kirkland clear wraps) and so the convenience factor is reduced. So I think that you will find that an alternative clear wrap product with a better system for dispensing & cutting is more enjoyable to use, and much more convenient.
summary: The wrap is fantastic, but the dispensing, cutting, & packaging is lackluster, making the Saran less convenient & time-saving

I find the 200 foot roll of Saran Cling Plus nearly impossible to extract from the box.  Pulling on the roll requires a force that breaks the box.  If you tape the box (with scotch packing tape), it just tears somewhere else.  Since the wrap clings well, fiddling with the box means that the wrap can fold over on itself, making it nearly impossible to untangle.  Since I buy this stuff to save time, this poor packaging erases most of the advantage.  Wax paper with a rubber band (my mom's solution) would be as fast and a lot cheaper.

Glad doesn't stick as well as this wrap, but it is much easier to manipulate in larger pieces, allowing you to cover food  fast.

One reviewer notes that Saran wrap sticks well in the microwave.  I'd be nervous about soft plastic adhering to my food in a microwave. There's a lot of buzz about chemicals in plastic leaching into food. To be safe, glass/china/paper are the containers of choice in the microwave. to prevent spattering, just put an upside down plate (china or paper) over the food being heated.

I like Saran wrap better than Glad, for some reason my husband and I believe it works better, it clings better and it doesn't melt as fast in the microwave as the others do. The price was right and it was delivered very quick.

reviewText: this has got to be the best cola i have ever had and it 10 time better than coca cola. it have a soft carbonation witch I like and a very complexed  flavor you'll get a fruity taste with some ginger at the back of you tongue at the end OMG its the best.its is highly recommended get this soda.

I came across this Fentimans soda locally, being sold either by the bottle or in four packs, and it intrigued me.  The glass bottle is an interesting design that reminds me of an English beer, the label has that classy old-timey look, and when you turn it to the important side (yes, the ingredients side is the important side), it hits you with stuff like... ginger... speedwell... juniper... yarrow--wait, does that say JUNIPER?

I popped it in the cart with a couple other varieties of the same brand--that Dandelion & Burdock stuff is an abomination, by the way--and saved it for a while, because I had a suspicion that I'd like it better than the others, if I liked any of it.

Well... you could have knocked me down with my first sip.  I was alone and literally said aloud, "Wow."  I have tried a lot of old timey, natural, and organic colas: Blue Sky, China Cola, Boylan's, GuS.  I try to avoid the HFCS.  There are some good ones out there: China Cola cherry, for instance (so hard to find these days); Boylan's Cane Cola.  Good stuff.  There are some not-so-good ones, too (Blue Sky, I'm looking at you; try harder.)

But this stuff?  This stuff is like the king of all colas: Among the rest of us, there might be some extraordinary individuals, but no one measures up to the king, and with so much going for him, it's almost silly to try to surpass his greatness.

The flavours in there are complex, with multiple things happening all at once--the bite of ginger, the softness of various herbs--but in the end, it's cola, and a damn good one--a GREAT one, I'd go even so far as to say.

I think it is a very good thing that this soda is not cheap.  If it was, I'd have a hard time ever drinking water again.

I really enjoyed Fentiman's Curiosity Cola when I was looking for something "different" in a drink.  The flavor is robust, full bodied, and like nothing else I've ever tasted in a soda.  The best way I could describe it is like Coke with a "kick" of spices.  Make sure to drink it ice cold. Yum.
summary: Nice, for a change of pace

reviewText: This soda will knock you out it's so good!  I bought one at a specialty shop and had to go back just for another soda! I realized later that the caffeine content is pretty high. The possibilities are endless!!!

I feel bad.  Like I'm cheating on my own other review.  But I have to be honest.  A year or two ago, I wrote a review praising another brand of "small batch" colas, proclaiming it as the "real" Real Thing.  I won't completely disown that review, but that was all before I tried Fentiman's.  Holy Moley.  I love Boylan's.  I love the Coca Cola from Mexico.  I loved Pepsi Throwback.  I even loved that complex, black sheep of colas, Red Bull cola.  Heck, I even enjoyed the strange, toasty flavor of Pepsi Raw... in small portions.  But this... this stuff is AMAZING!  Not too heavily carbonated.  Bursting with a variety of fruit flavors, this cola provides a multilayered tasting experience where the authentic cola taste gently unifies the other ingredients.  Sodas aren't supposed to taste this good.  Drinks like Fentimen's Curiosity Cola are why we fell in love with soda pop as kids.  For a special treat, it's well worth the price.  In a world of Scotch snobs, beer snobs, and wine snobs, this is the ultimate answer to what may emerge as the cola snob.  It is the Glenmorangie Scotch or Montecristo Cigar of colas.
summary: Of the new wave of microbrewed colas, this is easily the best!

50 plus years ago when I was a kid I have fond memories of having Del Monte Fresh Cut Golden Sweet Whole Kernel Corn from a can that did not look too much different than the one used now.  I remember fondly the aroma of corn wafting through the house which told me dinner was going to be especially good tonight. Del Monte Fresh Cut Golden Sweet Whole Kernel Corn was always delicious and I was a picky eater when it came to anything that was NOT Meat!  I hated veggies no matter how they were cooked.  I generally liked corn but, corn on the cob was just a bit too messy for me.  I have cerebral palsy so holding that cob and trying to eat the corn kerrels was a pure straight for the hyper-center of hell nightmare.

My parents were the inventive sort so they brought Del Monte Fresh Cut Golden Sweet Whole Kernel Corn in a can.  Corn served without the troublesome cob quickly became my favorite dish bar none. Del Monte Fresh Cut Golden Sweet Whole Kernel Corn was just sweet enough to taste good.  The best thing about Del Monte Fresh Cut Golden Sweet Whole Kernel Corn was the high quality never varied.  One can of Del Monte Fresh Cut Golden Sweet Whole Kernel Corn  tasted every bit as good as the next  Always fresh always good. Today I live near a specialty upscale market that has organic corn and its great.  So for giggles I brought a can of Del Monte Fresh Cut Golden Sweet Whole Kernel Corn just to see if it was still awesome as I remembered.  Turns out the Del Monte Fresh Cut Golden Sweet Whole Kernel Corn still holds its own in flavor and quality.  The kerrels are still plump and delicious not mangled like you find in most off brand canned corn.

No Del Monte Fresh Cut Golden Sweet Whole Kernel Corn is not good as fresh corn from a farmers market or one of the upscale organic markets BUT, it is still darn good.  Every so often I want great corn without fighting that darned cob with cerebral palsied fingers.  After a hard days work sometimes I just want corn without the hassle and when I do its gotta be Del Monte Fresh Cut Golden Sweet Whole Kernel Corn because; corn without the cob convenience should still tatse really good.

I am a devotee of coffee and chicory. My go-to brew is Community Coffee New Orleans Blend ("NOB"), but recently, I haven't received any email notification for specials, free shipping, etc. from CC. This caused me to look for a posible alternative to NOB.

CDM Coffee and Chicory ("CDM") is highly regarded,and Caf du Monde world-reknown. Sadly, for me, CDM is not an alternative to NOB.

CDM is available in vacuum-sealed bags (and cans) weighing 13 ounces; NOB is available in 1-lb vacuum sealed bags. Price-per-ounce is comparable, so this only affects storage space (CDM takes up more of it).

CDM is not as robust as NOR; 30g of CDM and 9 "Cuisinart Cups" (54 oz) of water makes a thin brew, while 30g of NOB and the same amount of water produces a brew that is hearty and strong. This is the stake in the heart for CDM. I cannot abide weak coffee.

I will keep a few bags of CDM in the pantry, but my quest for an alternative to NOB continues.

I usually go for products only available in salons because of my hair coloring and the keratin treatment I get in my hair. I used to work for a vendor of L'Oreal's parent company, Cosmair, and had access to their products at the company store years ago. I know some were quite good. I saw this and wanted to give it a try. I needed a deep conditioner for once a week to help my hair out in the colder weather. My hair is medium length past shoulders, naturally curls and is thick and coarse without keratin treatment every 12 weeks and product use. I was way overdue for a Brazilian Blowout and needed help!

I am really happy with this conditioner. It is leaves my hair feeling very smooth and silky after rinsing it out. The recommended use for it is 3-5 minutes and using it once a week. But, I use it longer when needed.

I have a small tip I have learned from my stylist years ago. If your hair is in dire need of a deep conditioning and you have the time, apply the conditioner, clip up your hair if it is long enough to fit it under a "processing cap" which is basically a cheap, plastic shower type cap that covers your hair. (You can get the on Amazon for a few dollars or the drugstore. I keep then handy for this and if I do any hair color touchups at home.) Then, leave it in your hair for 30 minutes or longer if you want. You will notice steam from under the cap from the moisture and heat of your head. When you are ready, rinse it as usual.

If you really, really want to deep condition your hair, I will share with you what I do. I have a bonnet dryer with a hard cap at home I use for gentle drying of curls, deep conditioning of my hair, or wearing a processing cap over root touch-ups to let the color sink in. They are $40 or less on Amazon and other stores and fold down for compact storage. In this case, I will sit under the dryer with conditioner on and processing cap over and read a book or play on my iPad and let the lower heat setting do it's work for about 20 minutes. It maximizes the conditioning for me and makes my coarse hair soft and with healthy shine again if my Brazilian blowout has washed out (after about 12-14 weeks.) If you don't have a bonnet dryer, a hair dryer will work to warm up your hair under the cap.

Anyhow, whether you use this 3-5 or 30 minutes to help repair and condition your hair, especially if it is damaged or over processed, it does a great job. I was happy with the price point for a quality hair product!

I booked my tickets on this mythical flavor expedition fully expecting to saunter my way onto an imaginary Napa Valley Wine Train with my destination being simply savory Chardonnay satisfaction.  I tore away the metal lid on their "microwaveable" container, lovingly ladled the contents into my trusty Rubbermaid bowl, and patiently passed gentle microwave radiation over the water molecules in the vicinity of this alleged mana from the gods for about three and a half minutes.

Imagine my immediate disappointment that begrudgingly yielded to shocked dissolutionment before firmly settling upon utter, absolute disenchantment as I tasted bite after bite of this gruel, the glowing smile of anticipation on my face being transformed through the waystation of confusion only to be ultimately eclipsed by the shadows of sadness.  My night train to Napa never even left the station.

If I could give this soup a half-star, I would.  The only reason I would give it even a half-star is because -- to distract myself from the existential crisis of my soul, I reckon -- I imagined that those little tiny pasta pebbles were so many edible rubber b.b.'s being shot down my throat and into the depths of my digestive system.

To be a fair and unbiased journalist, though, it's possible that this soup might have tasted better had I warmed it up a little more.  Regardless, I cannot abide this abhorrent concoction and my conscience will not stand for silence here.  You must be warned.  Only resort to this meal if you are in very dire straits.  Should you find yourself in some, I suppose this will tide you over until you are able to escape your merciless flavor captors.

Also, to that other reviewer that was disappointed that this does not taste like beef -- hello, it was chicken soup, it should not have tasted like beef, obviously.

WEIGHT: One pound of muscle burns six calories per pound per day. One pound of fat burns two calories per pound per day. That four calorie difference may not sound like much, but for most people, that's the difference between living lean and living obese and even morbidly obese (defined by those who are 100 or more pounds overweight). Cardiovascular exercise will result in weight loss, but it will come at a cost as 60% of the weight loss will be fat (that's good!) while the remaining 40% will come from muscle (that's really, really bad!). After the age of 20, the average person loses one-half to seven-tenths of a pound of muscle a year. That's 5 to 7 pounds a decade. After the age of 70, the average person loses 3 pounds of muscle--per year! As women approach menopause, the rate at which they lose muscle doubles, which is why so many women begin to gain weight right around that time of life. Why is this weight gain happening? It's simple--muscle loss. When you lose muscle, your metabolism is destroyed. Your successful weight loss formula is dieting plus strength training. Period. The body partially converts ALA to EPA and DHA. There is no proof what percent of ALA gets converted by human body to EPA or DHA. * Soluble fiber attracts water and turns to gel during digestion. This slows digestion. Soluble fiber is found in oat bran, barley, nuts, seeds, beans, lentils, peas, and some fruits and vegetables. reviewText:
I've been a huge fan of the True Citrus products for many years now. I've also told many friends about the products and now they all love them too. They used to only be available by online order directly from True Citrus, but I knew a great product like this would eventually be on the grocery shelves. Many retail outlets carry at least some of the products and now even Amazon has at least this one! :-)  Personally I drink gallons and gallons of the Regular Lemonade and Raspberry Lemonade in the 2qt size pouches. It's absolutely delicious and perhaps the only thing you can drink all day that's actually a bit better for you than plain water (there's a bit of vitamin C) and certainly no worse. There's no sugar or artificial sweeteners, there's real citrus and it tastes great! However, the particular true citrus product you are reviewing now is 100 small packets of lemon crystals. When they dissolve in liquid they are just as if you'd squeezed in about 1/4 of a lemon. Personally, I buy the 500 count boxes of True Lemon as well as True Lime, True Orange and True Grapefruit packets. How do so many get used that I need to buy 500 count boxes you ask? Well, first of all they basically last forever as long as you keep them dry. Second, they are REALLY GREAT IN BEER. I keep a half barrel on tap (or "draft" to some parts of the country) at all times in my garage. Friends and neighbors, not to mention myself, come over frequently to pour themselves a cold one and everyone agrees that adding a packet of a True Citrus flavor really enhances the taste. Different people have different preferences and that also varies by the type of beer. Personally, in general I like orange the best with a Weiss beer and I like lime the best with dark beers. Lemon goes well with either. Barrel after barrel, cup after cup, true citrus packets are steadily being consumed. If you're someone who loves the fruitiness of an IPA ( India Pale Ale) but doesn't like the bitterness of the hops, I suggest that you try this. You can either pay a lot for a good Belgian Abbey Ale... or you can take a good rich Lager or Farm Ale and add your own fruitiness. Here's how. Pour yourself a real mug of beer, meaning a FULL LITER (34 oz) like you get at Oktoberfest in Germany. Next add a packet of Lemon, a packet of Lime, a packet of Orange and lastly a packet of Grapefruit (I like grapefruit; skip it if you don't). You will end up with something that is amazingly refreshing and delicious. Seriously, if you do this with a good beer (not some cheap Pilsner) this is sooo good! New Glarus Brewery Spotted Cow is local to me and a great choice. It's a truly wonderful summer drink, but very enjoyable all year round. Now here's a tip to make it a bit easier. First pour about an ounce of beer into your glass, then add the true-citrus packets and swirl it around to dissolve and mix. Let the foam settle and finally pour in the remaining 33 oz's of beer. If you believe in science, take note that there is a huge body of research which indicates that enjoying one of these every day will give you a longer, healthier, happier life than those poor sots who drink nothing at all (Europeans know this all too well). Ahhhh bliss...  ;^)

...but if you insist on not using these in beer (poor soul) take solace in knowing that they do wonders for a glass of water or tea as well.
